{{ .Chart.Name }} {{ .Chart.AppVersion }} installed as release "{{ .Release.Name }}" in namespace "{{ .Release.Namespace }}".

Check the controller is running:

  kubectl -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} rollout status deployment/podpools-controller-manager
{{ if .Values.certmanager.enable }}
Requires cert-manager: the webhook's serving certificate is issued by cert-manager,
which must already be installed in the cluster. If the rollout hangs with the
webhook pod waiting on its cert, that is the likely cause. Install cert-manager,
or disable the webhook and cert-manager if you do not need admission webhooks.
{{ end -}}

The image is signed and carries a signed SLSA provenance attestation. Verify it:

  gh attestation verify oci://{{ .Values.controllerManager.container.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.controllerManager.container.image.tag | default .Chart.AppVersion }} \
    --repo negativecycle/podpool-controller

{{ if .Values.podSecurityStandards.enabled -}}
Namespace "{{ .Release.Namespace }}" enforces the {{ .Values.podSecurityStandards.standard }} Pod Security Standard.
{{ end -}}
{{ if .Values.policy.kyverno.enabled -}}
Admission verification (Kyverno) is ENABLED in {{ .Values.policy.kyverno.validationFailureAction }} mode.
{{- if eq .Values.policy.kyverno.validationFailureAction "Audit" }} It reports violations without blocking; review the policy report, then set policy.kyverno.validationFailureAction=Enforce.{{ end }}
{{- else -}}
Admission verification (Kyverno) is off. Enable it with --set policy.kyverno.enabled=true (requires Kyverno in the cluster).
{{- end }}
